title: Heat Transfer and its Effects
seo_title: Secondary 2 Science: Heat Transfer Worksheets (Lower Secondary Science with Answers)
standard_code: Secondary 2: Transfer of Heat Energy and its Effects
standard_text: State the kelvin as the SI unit of temperature; describe the effects and applications of expansion and contraction; explain heat transfer by conduction, convection and radiation and their applications; explain how surface colour, texture and temperature affect heat gained or lost by radiation; infer that heating changes volume and density and that materials conduct heat at different rates; recognise causes of global warming (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 science worksheets for Singapore students on heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation, conductors and insulators, expansion, kelvin and global warming. With answers.
key_big: Heat flows from hot to cold.
key_sub: Conduction in solids, convection in fluids, radiation through space.
body_html:
How to think about it

Heat flows from a hotter region to a colder region by conduction, convection or radiation.

  • Conduction: through solids, from particle to particle. Metals are good conductors; air, wood and plastic are insulators.
  • Convection: in liquids and gases. Heated fluid expands, becomes less dense and rises.
  • Radiation: infrared waves, even through a vacuum. Dull black surfaces absorb and emit best; shiny and white surfaces reflect.
  • Most substances expand on heating. Temperature in kelvin: K = °C + 273.
Example

What is 27 °C in kelvin?

27 + 273

Answer: 300 K

Example

Why does an air-conditioner work best high on a wall?

Cold air sinks

Answer: It sets up a convection current.

Common mistakes

  • Saying 'cold flows in'. Heat flows out of the warmer object.
  • Saying black surfaces reflect radiation. They absorb it.
  • Thinking convection happens in solids.
  • Calling air a good conductor. Trapped air is an insulator.

faq.q: What are the three ways heat is transferred?
faq.a: Conduction (through solids), convection (in liquids and gases) and radiation (infrared waves, even through a vacuum).
Dull black surfaces are the best absorbers and emitters. Shiny, white surfaces reflect radiation.

items.q: You feel warm sitting in sunshine. Which type of heat transfer is this mainly?
